figures.title: Fig. 2 analogue — Team size, disruption rank and citation counts (Stage 2)
figures.description: Design-weighted mean within-year disruption percentile (A) and median unique strictly postpublication citing works through 23 November 2026 (B), for 7,933 Columbia OpenAlex works with at least one such citer. Unweighted stratum n is below each team size; dotted line separates exact sizes from pooled bands. Error bars show pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from 1,000 focal-work replacement draws within each original stratum with original inverse-inclusion weights and reranking; no finite-population correction, including in the fully sampled 51–100 stratum. Trends are not strictly monotone. For 51–100 authors the median is 39 citing works [31,46], n=477.

reviews.summary: Both panels support C1 as an overall, nonmonotonic pattern: larger teams tend to have lower mean disruption percentiles and higher median citation counts, with both patterns extending into the pooled 51–100-author band. The displayed counts sum to 7,933, the visible singleton estimates match T66, and the fully sampled band has nonzero intervals under the stated no-FPC bootstrap.

issues.problem: The phrase “1,000 focal-work replacement draws” could be read as 1,000 individual works rather than 1,000 bootstrap replicates.
issues.fix: Say “1,000 bootstrap replicates, each resampling the original number of focal works with replacement within every stratum.” Retain the notes on weighting, reranking, and no finite-population correction.

issues.problem: The equally spaced categories include both exact team sizes and pooled bands, so the connecting slopes do not represent change per additional author.
issues.fix: Add a short caption note that the x-axis uses equally spaced categories and that the extension to 100 authors is represented by the pooled 51–100 band.

figures.title: Extended figure — Signed raw disruption distributions (Stage 2)
figures.description: Inverse-inclusion-weighted empirical CDF of signed raw D for one, ten and 51–100 authors (600, 624 and 477 Columbia OpenAlex works with at least one distinct citing work in the postpublication window ending 23 November 2026). Display range is −0.1 to 0.1 on a symmetric log scale; zero is the sign boundary between development (negative) and disruption (positive). Pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap bands: in each of 1,000 replicates resample the original number of focal works with replacement within each original stratum, including 51–100, without a finite-population correction. The raw score for most works is close to zero; the curves differ around zero. Source: T67.

reviews.summary: The weighted CDFs support C2 by showing how the share of works on either side of zero differs across the three team-size groups, rather than reporting only mean scores. The plotted counts match the revised eligibility rule, and all three groups, including the fully sampled stratum, have visible pointwise bootstrap bands.

issues.problem: The caption notes that the curves differ near zero but leaves the main comparison implicit. Because the CDF includes zero, its height at zero is not the share of works with negative scores.
issues.fix: State that the weighted share with D ≤ 0 rises from about 56% for solo authors to 82% for ten authors and 91% for 51–100 authors. Note that each jump at zero represents works with D = 0.

issues.problem: The accompanying P1 version 1 record describes the superseded sample and variance method, which could be mistaken for the provenance of the displayed figure.
issues.fix: Label P1 version 1 as superseded and make sure the exported Stage 2 figure record points to T67 and the no-FPC bootstrap.

figures.title: Fig. 3 analogue — Team size and disruption across citation impact (Stage 2)
figures.description: Inverse-inclusion-weighted mean within-year disruption percentile for 7,933 Columbia OpenAlex works with at least one distinct strictly postpublication citing work through 23 November 2026. Higher D percentiles indicate greater disruption; the horizontal line marks percentile 50, the vertical line separates exact sizes and grouped sizes. Impact bands use weighted midranks; unweighted n are in the legend. Pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap intervals: in each of 1,000 replicates resample the original number of focal works with replacement in each original stratum, including 51–100, with no finite-population correction; recompute D and impact ranks and bins jointly. For teams of 1–10, slopes in percentile points per author doubling: bottom half −2.50 [−3.39, −1.64], n=3,277; middle band −1.22 [−2.54, 0.48], n=2,476; top decile +0.23 [−4.33, 3.37], n=457. Top-minus-bottom +2.73 [−1.89, 6.00], n=3,734. The bottom-half decline is supported, but not a decline at every impact level or a stronger decline at high impact. Larger-team bands are descriptive. Source: T68.

reviews.summary: The figure clearly evaluates C3 without overstating the result. Among teams of 1–10 authors, only the bottom impact band shows a clear decline in disruption with team size. The top-minus-bottom slope contrast is imprecise and does not support a stronger decline at high impact. The caption documents the cited-work restriction and the within-stratum bootstrap without a finite-population correction, including for the fully sampled stratum.

issues.problem: The caption specifies weighted midranks but does not explicitly say which citation measure is ranked to define impact.
issues.fix: State that impact bands are based on within-publication-year weighted midranks of the number of distinct strictly postpublication citing works observed through 23 November 2026.

figures.title: Fig. 3 analogue — Negative slopes predominate in supported fields and subfields (Stage 2)
figures.description: Within-year D percentile slopes per doubling of team size for Columbia OpenAlex works with 1–10 authors and at least one unique strictly postpublication citing work through 23 November 2026. Dots and bars are inverse-inclusion-weighted slopes and pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap intervals; resample focal works with replacement within original strata (1,000 replicates), rerank and apply no finite-population correction, including the fully sampled stratum. Unweighted n shown for each field. Support requires n≥30, ≥5 in each of the 1–2 and 5–10 author bands and ≥4 distinct sizes. Table weights groups equally and holds each domain’s observed supported set fixed in resamples. Slopes are negative in 14/20 fields and 24/34 subfields; only one journal meets support, so no generalization to most journals.

reviews.summary: The Stage 2 figure matches the cited-work analysis in T69 and T70 and reports the within-stratum bootstrap without a finite-population correction. It supports C4 only in part: estimated slopes are negative in 14 of 20 supported fields and 24 of 34 supported subfields, but the pattern is not universal, and the single supported journal cannot establish a pattern across most journals.

issues.problem: The caption uses D without defining it or explaining what a negative slope means.
issues.fix: Define D as the disruption index and state that a negative slope means larger teams rank lower on disruption within publication year.

issues.problem: The journal row's “100%” gives visual prominence to a result based on one supported journal, even though the caption correctly rules out generalization.
issues.fix: Show “1 of 1” without the percentage and keep the 0%–100% interval.

figures.title: Fig. 4 analogue — Empirical distributions of reference age and popularity (Stage 2)
figures.description: Stage-2 update of P12, preserving its empirical panels and geometry. Among Columbia OpenAlex works with at least one unique postpublication citing work through 23 November 2026, the curves pool deduplicated focal–reference pairs, applying the focal inverse-inclusion weight to every edge. For 1, 10 and 51–100 authors, respectively, A uses 22,001/34,531/43,548 edges and B uses 22,149/34,613/43,772 edges; both use 597/624/477 focal works with available metadata. Ribbons are pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from 1,000 focal-work replacement samples within the original team-size strata, including 51–100, with no finite-population correction. A includes same-year ages, excludes negative ages and displays thresholds through 100 years. B uses current global citation totals, not counts at focal publication; the axis is linear up to one and logarithmic above (no observed zeros). Both larger groups cite newer and generally more highly cited references than solo works; their popularity curves are close. These are empirical comparisons of the groups shown, not fitted curves. Separate updated fit evidence (T76/T77) shows positive geometric age-decay contrast for 10 versus solo, inconclusive citation-tail exponent contrast at counts ≥50, and notable empirical–fitted CDF gaps.

reviews.summary: The revised P12 clearly shows that both larger-team groups cite newer and generally more highly cited references than solo works, while the two larger groups have similar popularity curves. The caption documents the citation eligibility rule, edge weighting, and focal-work bootstrap without a finite-population correction. The figure is ready for the report as the empirical component of C5.

issues.problem: The curves support the empirical part of C5 for the three groups shown, but do not establish differences in fitted distribution parameters. The caption flags this distinction, but the results text could still overstate the evidence.
issues.fix: Present T76/T77 alongside the figure in the C5 subsection. Distinguish the supported age-decay contrast for 10-author versus solo works from the inconclusive citation-tail exponent contrast.

issues.problem: The caption names the fit artifacts but does not cite the updated source for the empirical curves, intervals, and sample counts.
issues.fix: Cite T75 in the caption for the plotted estimates, ribbons, and counts.
